subject: Health and Human Development
name: Health and Human Development, Units 1 and 2
about: VCE, Health, nutrition, development and the health system
syllabus: VCE Health and Human Development Study Design (from 2025), Units 1 and 2

points.title: Definitions of health
points.brief: Health has been defined in different ways, from the absence of disease to the World Health Organization's complete physical, mental and social wellbeing.

points.title: Dimensions of health and wellbeing
points.brief: Health has physical, mental, social, emotional and spiritual dimensions, which are linked so a change in one affects the others.

points.title: Health as dynamic and subjective
points.brief: Health changes over time (dynamic) and each person judges their own differently (subjective).

points.title: Prerequisites for health
points.brief: The WHO lists conditions needed for health, peace, shelter, education, food, income, a stable ecosystem, sustainable resources, social justice and equity.

points.title: Youth perspectives on health
points.brief: Young people often link health to fitness, appearance, friendships and independence, which can differ from what adults stress.

points.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander views of health
points.brief: Health is seen holistically, linking the person to family, community, culture, Country and spirit.

points.title: Measuring health status
points.brief: Incidence, prevalence, morbidity, hospitalisation, burden of disease, mortality and life expectancy describe how healthy a group is.

points.title: The health status of Australia's youth
points.brief: Most young Australians rate their health highly, but mental health conditions, injury and overweight are common concerns.

points.title: Factors affecting youth health
points.brief: Peer group, family, education, income and health literacy help explain why health differs between young people.

points.title: Areas needing action
points.brief: Health data points to the areas of youth health that most need action, such as mental health, injury and alcohol use.

points.title: Programs for youth health
points.brief: Government and non-government programs, such as on road safety or mental health, aim to improve young people's health.

points.title: A youth health focus
points.brief: Studying one issue, such as mental health or body image, shows its effect on each dimension of health and its trends in the data.

points.title: Risk and protective factors
points.brief: Risk factors make a health problem more likely; protective factors make it less likely or soften its effects.

points.title: The costs of a health issue
points.brief: A health issue has direct costs such as treatment, indirect costs such as lost work, and intangible costs such as pain and stress.

points.title: Youth advocacy
points.brief: Young people can act personally and in their communities to speak up for better and fairer health.

points.title: Carbohydrates
points.brief: The body's main source of energy. Complex carbohydrates and fibre release energy slowly and help digestion.

points.title: Fats
points.brief: Fats store energy, insulate and help absorb some vitamins. Unsaturated fats are healthier than saturated and trans fats.

points.title: Protein
points.brief: Protein builds and repairs tissue and makes enzymes and hormones. It comes from meat, fish, eggs, dairy, legumes and nuts.

points.title: Water
points.brief: Water carries nutrients, removes wastes and controls body temperature. Most of the body is water.

points.title: Vitamins
points.brief: Vitamins C and D and folate are needed in small amounts, for processes such as healing, bone growth and healthy pregnancy.

points.title: Minerals
points.brief: Minerals such as calcium for bones, iron for carrying oxygen and sodium for fluid balance are needed in small amounts.

points.title: The Australian Dietary Guidelines
points.brief: Five guidelines for healthy eating, including enjoying a range of foods and limiting saturated fat, added salt, sugar and alcohol.

points.title: The Australian Guide to Healthy Eating
points.brief: A plate graphic showing the five food groups in the proportions to eat each day.

points.title: The Healthy Eating Pyramid and Health Star Rating
points.brief: The Healthy Eating Pyramid shows how much of each food group to eat, and the Health Star Rating compares packaged foods.

points.title: Judging nutrition information
points.brief: Good nutrition advice comes from qualified sources, is backed by evidence and does not sell a quick fix.

points.title: Influences on food choices
points.brief: Taste, cost, family, culture, convenience, knowledge and commercial factors can help or hinder healthy eating for young people.

points.title: Marketing food to young people
points.brief: Food companies target young people with social media, influencers, sponsorship and packaging, often for less healthy foods.

points.title: Growth and development compared
points.brief: Growth is a change in size. Development is a change in ability and complexity, across physical, social, emotional and intellectual areas.

points.title: Stages of the lifespan
points.brief: Life runs through stages such as prenatal, infancy, childhood, youth, adulthood and old age, each with typical changes.

points.title: Perceptions of youth and adulthood
points.brief: What it means to be young or an adult differs between people and cultures, beyond age alone.

points.title: Physical development
points.brief: Changes in the body and its systems, such as the growth spurt and puberty in youth.

points.title: Social and emotional development
points.brief: Learning to relate to others and to understand and manage feelings, which change as people form new relationships.

points.title: Intellectual development
points.brief: Growth in thinking, memory, language and problem solving, which continues through life.

points.title: The move from youth to adulthood
points.brief: Becoming an adult brings independence, work, relationships and new responsibilities, which can affect health.

points.title: Healthy and respectful relationships
points.brief: Respect, trust, honesty and safety mark a healthy relationship, which supports health and development.

points.title: Becoming a parent
points.brief: Parenthood changes responsibilities, relationships and finances, and can add stress.

points.title: Support for parents
points.brief: Family, friends, maternal and child health nurses and parenting services help new parents.

points.title: Prenatal development
points.brief: From fertilisation, a baby develops through the germinal, embryonic and fetal stages.

points.title: Risks before birth
points.brief: A mother's diet, smoking and alcohol during pregnancy can affect a baby's development; good nutrition and care protect it.

points.title: Development in infancy and early childhood
points.brief: Rapid physical, social, emotional and intellectual development happens in the first years of life.

points.title: Early life experiences
points.brief: Care, nutrition and stress early in life shape health and development for decades.

points.title: Health across generations
points.brief: Parents' health and circumstances affect their children's health, and so on to the next generation.

points.title: GPs, allied and alternative health
points.brief: GPs are usually the first stop. Allied health includes physiotherapists and psychologists; alternative health includes naturopathy.

points.title: Medicare
points.brief: Australia's public health insurance, funded by taxes and the Medicare levy, which covers or subsidises doctors, tests and public hospital care.

points.title: The Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme
points.brief: The PBS subsidises many prescription medicines so they cost less for everyone, and less again for concession card holders.

points.title: Private health insurance
points.brief: Optional insurance that covers private hospital care and extras such as dental, encouraged by rebates and levies.

points.title: Local services for young people
points.brief: Community services such as headspace, school wellbeing staff and youth centres support every dimension of youth health.

points.title: Access to health services
points.brief: Cost, location, confidentiality worries, knowledge and culture affect whether young people use health services and information.

points.title: Rights and responsibilities in health care
points.brief: Patients have rights to privacy, confidentiality and to know how their health data is stored and shared, and responsibilities such as giving honest information.

points.title: Digital health
points.brief: Websites, online practitioners and health apps make information and care easier to reach, but quality and privacy vary.

points.title: Complaints and redress
points.brief: Patients can complain to the provider, then to bodies such as the Health Complaints Commissioner, if care goes wrong.
